content.title: How to Watch Lakers vs. Mavericks, Rockets vs. Warriors - Sunday Night Basketball on NBC
content.text: We're in the final days of the 2025-2026 NBA regular season. Less than two weeks remain for teams to cement their playoff spots and prepare for the postseason, and we're entering the NBA on NBC's final week of regular season coverage. For fans, that means hoping your favorite team gets a good playoff position (if they're eligible), but it also means taking advantage of as much NBA action as possible while the getting's good.How to WatchThis week on the 2025-2026 season finale of Sunday Night Basketball, NBC Sports will close out your Easter Sunday with a doubleheader of NBA action featuring three different playoff bound teams trying to finish the season strong and healthy in preparation for the postseason. Let's take a closer look at this Sunday's tipoffs.RELATED: How Do the NBA Playoffs and Play-In Tournament Work in 2026?Who's playing on Sunday Night Basketball on NBC and Peacock this week?The Easter Sunday edition of Sunday Night Basketball begins at 7:30 p.m. ET, as the Los Angeles Lakers head to Dallas to face the Mavericks live from the American Airlines Center. The action continues at 10 p.m., as the Houston Rockets fly West to face the Golden State Warriors in a battle of Western Conference powers.Mike Tirico will call the action for Lakers vs. Mavericks, with analysis from Jamal Crawford and courtside reporting from Ashley ShahAhmadi. Noah Eagle will handle play-by-play duties for Rockets vs. Warriors, with the legendary Reggie Miller alongside him in the booth and courtside reporting from Grant Liffmann. Both games will air live on NBC in their respective regions, and stream live on Peacock regardless of location, so you'll be able to catch all the action from your devices. And be sure to tune in early at 6:30 p.m. ET for Basketball Night in America, NBC Sports' live NBA pregame show hosted by Ahmad Fareed.RELATED: The Full 2025-2026 Schedule of NBA Games on NBC and PeacockWhat to expect from this week's Sunday Night Basketball match-upsIn terms of the stakes, three of the teams playing Sunday night already know they're playoff bound, while one already knows they're eliminated.Los Angeles Lakers vs. Dallas MavericksIn Dallas, the Mavericks are licking their wounds from a rough season which saw the loss of Kyrie Irving amid the rise of number one overall draft pick Cooper Flagg. Flagg's getting valuable minutes this season, but for the Mavericks as a whole, this can be marked up as a rebuilding year, a chance to regroup with another strong draft and to try again this fall. The Lakers, on the other hand, still have something to play for in a more immediate sense. They've clinched a playoff berth, but seeding is still up in the air, and they're virtually neck and neck with the Nuggets in the Western Conference standings. They need to keep winning to hold onto potential seeding advantages, but they may have to do it without their leading scorer and passer, Luka Dončić, who went down with a hamstring injury on April 2. While he's listed as a game time decision, there's a chance that even if he feels OK the Lakers will sit him to preserve his energy for the postseason. That leaves the Mavericks with an opening, and that could make this game interesting. Houston Rockets vs. Golden State WarriorsOut in California, the Warriors have clinched a Play-In Tournament berth, and their position is more-or-less set, leaving them to hang on and preserve their strength. The Rockets, on the other hand, are still looking at ways to improve their seeding. They've got an automatic berth in the West, but they're sandwiched between the Nuggets and the Timberwolves in the standings, with just a couple of games separating the teams. That means if they finish strong, they could have an easier time with the first round of the Playoffs, so Kevin Durant and the rest of the Rockets crew will be doing their best to make that happen.
